items.title: Section: The Fourth and Fifth Summary Verses Open Together — Nine Topics Spanning the Remainder of the Chapter

items.zh: 復次，嗢拕南曰：諸施設建立、一切法尋思、及如實遍智、如是諸無量、說法果勝利、大乘性、與攝，菩薩十，應知建立諸名號。
items.en: Furthermore, a summary verse states: "Establishing designations; investigating all phenomena; and genuine, complete wisdom; the various immeasurables thus; the fruit and benefit of teaching the truth; the great vehicle's nature and what it comprises; ten kinds of bodhisattva one should know; establishing the various titles."

items.title: Section: Establishing Designations Opens — Only the Buddha and Bodhisattvas Can Truly Establish Them, Beginning With the Establishing of Teaching Itself

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩略有四種施設建立，唯有如來及諸菩薩能正施設、能正建立；非餘一切若天、若人、若諸沙門、若婆羅門，唯除聞已。何等為四？一者、法施設建立，二者、諦施設建立，三者、理施設建立，四者、乘施設建立。云何名法施設建立？謂佛所說素呾纜等十二分教，次第結集、次第安置、次第制立，是名為法施設建立。
items.en:
This means that bodhisattvas, in brief, have four kinds of establishing designations. Only the tathagatas and bodhisattvas are capable of correctly designating and correctly establishing these; no other being at all — whether a god, a human, a renunciant, or a brahmin — can do so, except by first hearing it from them. What are these four? First, establishing through teaching. Second, establishing through truths. Third, establishing through principles. Fourth, establishing through vehicles.
What is called establishing through teaching? It means that the twelve divisions of scripture spoken by the Buddha — discourse and the rest — are compiled, arranged, and instituted in proper sequence. This is called establishing through teaching.
Commentary: Regarding "compiled ... arranged ... instituted in proper sequence" — undistortedly establishing names, phrases, and syllables in their proper sequence is called compiling in sequence. Undistortedly accomplishing the wisdom of hearing, reflecting, and cultivating is called arranging in sequence. Undistortedly relying on the trainings of moral discipline, concentration, and wisdom is called instituting in sequence.

items.title: Section: Establishing Through Truths Opens — Boundless in Number, Beginning With the Single Truth and the Two Truths

items.zh: 云何名諦施設建立？謂無量種。或立一諦。謂不虛妄義，唯有一諦，無第二故。或立二諦。一、世俗諦，二、勝義諦。
items.en:
What is called establishing through truths? It means there are boundless kinds. Some establish a single truth: the meaning of non-falsity, in which there is only one truth, since there is no second.
Commentary: Regarding "some establish a single truth" — this refers to the non-conceptually-established truth, one should understand. For the suchness of all phenomena is called the meaning of non-falsity.
Some establish two truths: first, conventional truth; second, ultimate truth.

items.title: Section: The Three Truths Mapped Onto the Five Categories, and the Familiar Four Noble Truths

items.zh: 或立三諦。一、相諦，二、語諦，三、用諦。或立四諦。一、苦諦，二、集諦，三、滅諦，四、道諦。
items.en:
Some establish three truths: first, the truth of characteristics; second, the truth of language; third, the truth of function.
Commentary: Regarding "some establish three truths" — among the great vehicle's five categories, characteristic is the truth of characteristics, name is the truth of language, and discrimination together with correct wisdom together are this truth of function.
Some establish four truths: first, the truth of suffering; second, the truth of origination; third, the truth of cessation; fourth, the truth of the path.

items.title: Section: The Five Truths of Cause, Result, Knowing Wisdom, Known Object, and the Supreme, and the Six Truths Pairing True With False

items.zh: 或立五諦。一、因諦，二、果諦，三、智諦，四、境諦，五、勝諦。或立六諦。一、諦諦，二、妄諦，三、應遍知諦，四、應永斷諦，五、應作證諦，六、應修習諦。
items.en:
Some establish five truths: first, the truth of cause; second, the truth of result; third, the truth of wisdom; fourth, the truth of the object; fifth, the supreme truth.
Commentary: Regarding "some establish five truths" — origination and the path are called the truth of cause. Suffering and cessation are called the truth of result. The wisdom that knows these is called the truth of wisdom. The object that wisdom knows is called the truth of the object. What the noble ones realise, together with the wisdom that realises it, is called the supreme truth.
Some establish six truths: first, the truth that is truly true; second, the truth that is false; third, the truth to be fully known; fourth, the truth to be forever severed; fifth, the truth to be personally realised; sixth, the truth to be cultivated.
Commentary: Regarding "some establish six truths" — cessation and the path are called the truth that is truly true. Suffering and origination are called the truth that is false. That suffering should be fully known is called the truth to be fully known. That origination should be forever severed is called the truth to be forever severed. That cessation should be personally realised is called the truth to be personally realised. That the path should be cultivated is called the truth to be cultivated.

items.title: Section: The Seven Truths — Craving's Savour, Its Danger, Renunciation, the Nature of Phenomena, Resolute Understanding, and the Noble Versus the Ignorant

items.zh: 或立七諦。一、愛味諦，二、過患諦，三、出離諦，四、法性諦，五、勝解諦，六、聖諦，七、非聖諦。
items.en:
Some establish seven truths: first, the truth of craving's savour; second, the truth of danger; third, the truth of renunciation; fourth, the truth of the nature of phenomena; fifth, the truth of resolute understanding; sixth, the truth of the noble; seventh, the truth of the ignorant.
Commentary: Regarding "some establish seven truths" — designating the defiling conditions of conditioned phenomena is called the truth of craving's savour. Designating the purifying conditions of conditioned phenomena is called the truth of danger. The purification of conditioned phenomena is called the truth of renunciation. Truly and correctly knowing the nature of this or that phenomenon is called the truth of the nature of phenomena. The resolute understanding that arises from contemplating it is called the truth of resolute understanding. Those who have already seen the truth, realising the nature of phenomena without contradiction, are called the truth of the noble. Ignorant worldly people, whose awareness of these phenomena likewise shows no contradiction to their own view, are called the truth of the ignorant.

items.title: Section: The Eight Truths — Suffering Unfolded Into Its Three Kinds, and the Fourfold Movement of Samsara and Its Purification

items.zh: 或立八諦。一、行苦性諦，二、壞苦性諦，三、苦苦性諦，四、流轉諦，五、還滅諦，六、雜染諦，七、清淨諦，八、正加行諦。
items.en:
Some establish eight truths: first, the truth of the suffering of formations; second, the truth of the suffering of change; third, the truth of suffering itself; fourth, the truth of flowing; fifth, the truth of returning cessation; sixth, the truth of defilement; seventh, the truth of purity; eighth, the truth of correct effort.
Commentary: Regarding "some establish eight truths" — the first three may be understood as given. Based on these three kinds of suffering, flowing through the three realms is called the truth of flowing. Their eternal cessation, final and complete escape, is called the truth of returning cessation. The three sufferings continuing to flow is called the truth of defilement. The three sufferings returning to cessation is called the truth of purity. The skilful means of purification is called the truth of correct effort.

items.title: Section: The Nine Truths — Craving for Existence and Craving for Non-Existence, and the Two Kinds of Nirvana

items.zh: 或立九諦。一、無常諦，二、苦諦，三、空諦，四、無我諦，五、有愛諦，六、無有愛諦，七、彼斷方便諦，八、有餘依涅槃諦，九、無餘依涅槃諦。
items.en:
Some establish nine truths: first, the truth of impermanence; second, the truth of suffering; third, the truth of emptiness; fourth, the truth of no-self; fifth, the truth of craving for existence; sixth, the truth of craving for non-existence; seventh, the truth of the means of severing these; eighth, the truth of nirvana with remainder; ninth, the truth of nirvana without remainder.
Commentary: Regarding "the truth of craving for existence, the truth of craving for non-existence" and the like — seeking a rebirth one finds pleasing and performing meritorious deeds towards that end is called craving for existence. Relying on craving for non-existence and performing meritorious deeds, or deeds fixed towards the form and formless realms, towards that end is called craving for non-existence. The meaning is as explained in the Sutra on the Supreme Approach to Discerning Dependent Origination. Severing the two kinds of ignorance underlying both craving for existence and craving for non-existence, through the decisively superior path, is called the truth of the means of severing these.

items.title: Section: The Ten Truths Mapped Onto the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination, Closing Establishing Through Truths — and Establishing Through Principles Briefly Opens

items.zh: 或立十諦。一、逼切苦諦，二、財位匱乏苦諦，三、界不平和苦諦，四、所愛變壞苦諦，五、麁重苦諦，六、業諦，七、煩惱諦，八、聽聞正法、如理作意諦，九、正見諦，十、正見果諦。如是等類，名菩薩諦施設建立，若廣分別當知無量。云何名理施設建立？謂四道理。此廣分別如前應知。
items.en:
Some establish ten truths: first, the truth of compelling suffering; second, the truth of the suffering of scarce wealth and standing; third, the truth of the suffering of bodily imbalance; fourth, the truth of the suffering of the beloved's decay; fifth, the truth of the suffering of coarse, latent tendency; sixth, the truth of karma; seventh, the truth of affliction; eighth, the truth of hearing the true teaching and correctly reflecting upon it; ninth, the truth of correct view; tenth, the truth of the result of correct view.
Classifications such as these are called a bodhisattva's establishing of truths. If analysed extensively, one should understand that they are truly boundless in number.
What is called establishing through principles? It refers to the four kinds of reasoning. Their extensive analysis should be understood exactly as given earlier.

items.title: Section: Establishing Through Vehicles Opens — Seven Aspects of the Disciple's Vehicle

items.zh: 云何名乘施設建立？謂聲聞乘及獨覺乘、無上大乘，如是三種，一一各由七種行相施設建立，是名為乘施設建立。初聲聞乘七行相者，一、於四聖諦無顛倒慧，二、此慧所依，三、此慧所緣，四、此慧伴類，五、此慧作業，六、此慧資糧，七、此慧得果。當知由此七種行相施設建立，諸聲聞乘無不周備。
items.en:
What is called establishing through vehicles? It means the disciple's vehicle, the solitary-awakener's vehicle, and the unsurpassed great vehicle. Each of these three is established through seven aspects. This is called establishing through vehicles.
The disciple's vehicle has seven aspects: first, undistorted wisdom regarding the four noble truths; second, what this wisdom depends on; third, what this wisdom takes as its object; fourth, this wisdom's companions; fifth, this wisdom's function; sixth, this wisdom's provisions; seventh, this wisdom's resulting fruit. One should understand that through these seven aspects, the entire disciple's vehicle is established with nothing lacking.
Commentary: Regarding "what this wisdom depends on, what this wisdom takes as its object" and the like — the disciple's own lineage is called what the wisdom depends on. The teaching of the four noble truths is called what the wisdom takes as its object. The factors of awakening are called this wisdom's companions. Severing the afflictions is called this wisdom's function. Hearing the true teaching, reflecting, and cultivating are called this wisdom's provisions. The four fruits of renunciate life are called this wisdom's resulting fruit.

items.title: Section: The Solitary Awakener's Vehicle Follows by Analogy — the Unsurpassed Great Vehicle's Own Seven Aspects, Culminating in Unsurpassed Awakening

items.zh: 如聲聞乘七種行相施設建立，其獨覺乘，當知亦爾。無上大乘七行相者，一、緣離言說事，一切法中所有真如，無分別平等性出離慧；二、此慧所依；三、此慧所緣；四、此慧伴類；五、此慧作業；六、此慧資糧；七、此慧得果。當知由此七種行相施設建立，無上大乘無不周備。
items.en:
Just as the disciple's vehicle is established through these seven aspects, one should understand that the solitary awakener's vehicle is likewise established.
The unsurpassed great vehicle has seven aspects: first, undistorted, liberating wisdom taking as its object what is beyond language, the suchness present in all phenomena, non-discriminating and equalizing; second, what this wisdom depends on; third, what this wisdom takes as its object; fourth, this wisdom's companions; fifth, this wisdom's function; sixth, this wisdom's provisions; seventh, this wisdom's resulting fruit. One should understand that through these seven aspects, the unsurpassed great vehicle is established with nothing lacking.
Commentary: Regarding "taking as its object what is beyond language" and the like — the selflessness of all phenomena is called the suchness present in all phenomena. Its nature being beyond language is likewise called what is beyond language. The wisdom of the selflessness of phenomena arising by taking this as its object, which, regarding both the nature beyond language and the nature merely provisionally designated in all phenomena, remains entirely equal without giving rise to any discrimination, and thereby attains liberation from the cognitive obscuration, is called non-discriminating, equalizing, liberating wisdom. The great vehicle's own lineage is called what this wisdom depends on. The extensive teaching is called what this wisdom takes as its object. The various factors of awakening are called this wisdom's companions. The capacity to sever the two obscurations is called this wisdom's function. Extensive hearing, reflecting, and cultivating are called this wisdom's provisions. Unsurpassed awakening is called this wisdom's resulting fruit.

items.title: Section: The Conclusion — All Establishing Designations by Every Buddha and Bodhisattva, Past, Present, and Future, Reduces to Just These Four

items.zh: 過去、未來、現在諸佛及諸菩薩所有無倒施設建立，若曾所作、若當所作、若今所作，一切皆由如是四事。除此無有若過若增。
items.en: Whatever undistorted establishing of designations belongs to the buddhas and bodhisattvas of the past, future, and present — whether already accomplished, yet to be accomplished, or being accomplished now — all of it is entirely comprised within these four matters. Beyond these, there is nothing exceeding them, and nothing that could be added to them.

items.title: Section: The Four Investigations Open — Name, Thing, Provisionally-Posited Intrinsic Nature, and Provisionally-Posited Distinction

items.zh: 又諸菩薩為得四種如實遍知，於一切法起四尋思。何等為四？一、名尋思，二、事尋思，三、自性假立尋思，四、差別假立尋思。如是四種若廣分別，應知如前真實義品。
items.en:
Furthermore, bodhisattvas, in order to attain four kinds of genuine, complete wisdom regarding all phenomena, give rise to four kinds of investigation regarding all phenomena. What are these four? First, investigation of names. Second, investigation of things. Third, investigation of provisionally-posited intrinsic nature. Fourth, investigation of provisionally-posited distinction.
These four, if analysed extensively, should be understood exactly as explained earlier in the Chapter on Genuine Reality.

items.title: Section: The Four Kinds of Genuine Wisdom Open — Wisdom Drawn From Investigating Names

items.zh: 又諸菩薩略有四種，於一切法如實遍知。一、名尋思所引如實遍知，二、事尋思所引如實遍知，三、自性假立尋思所引如實遍知，四、差別假立尋思所引如實遍
items.en: Furthermore, bodhisattvas have, in brief, four kinds of genuine, complete wisdom regarding all phenomena. What are these four? First, genuine, complete wisdom drawn from investigating names. Second, genuine, complete wisdom drawn from investigating things. Third, genuine, complete wisdom drawn from investigating provisionally-posited intrinsic nature. Fourth, genuine, complete wisdom drawn from investigating provisionally-posited distinction.

items.title: Section: Wisdom Drawn From Investigating Provisionally-Posited Distinction — Neither Existent Nor Nonexistent, Without Duality — Closing the Four Kinds of Genuine Wisdom

items.zh: 知。如是四種若廣分別，應知如前真實義品。
items.en:
Fourth, genuine, complete wisdom drawn from investigating provisionally-posited distinction. Having investigated that provisionally-posited distinction is nothing but the provisionally-posited distinction itself, a bodhisattva genuinely penetrates that the distinctions arising upon dependently-arisen phenomena are likewise merely provisionally posited, and that every such distinction is, in truth, non-dual.
These four, if analysed extensively, should be understood exactly as explained earlier in the Chapter on Genuine Reality.

blocks.text: The fourth and fifth summary verses list nine topics for the rest of the chapter. Today: how the Buddha and bodhisattvas "establish" the teaching, with truths counted from one to ten, and a return to the four investigations of fascicle 36.

Teaching, truths, principles, vehicles: only tathāgatas and bodhisattvas can rightly establish them; others only after hearing. Master Cháng Bǎi: others can only repeat what they heard. On "compiling, arranging, instituting": compiling refers to sūtras, arranging to treatises, instituting to vinaya.
"Some establish a single truth: the meaning of non-falsity; only one truth, since there is no second." Venerable Miào Jìng: this praises suchness as not false, truly real.
Venerable Miào Jìng: we ordinary people deal in two things, characteristics and names; that is where we operate. Without names you could not speak.
Both lecturers: the truth of resolute understanding is the cause; the truth of renunciation is its result.
Venerable Miào Jìng: there is no self in form, feeling, perception, formations, consciousness: the truth of emptiness. Apart from them there is also no self: the truth of no-self.

Master Cháng Bǎi: suffering presses like a knife cutting, hence "compelling". Venerable Miào Jìng: the ten truths are still the four truths, with suffering spelled out in more detail; establishing through principles differs from establishing through truths only in name.

"First, undistorted wisdom on the four noble truths; then its basis, object, companions, function, provisions, and fruit." Venerable Miào Jìng: this wisdom is not alone; as it develops, it has companions.
Venerable Miào Jìng: the buddha-nature within beings is the basis of liberating wisdom. Master Cháng Bǎi: the seed of bodhicitta is its basis.

Of names, of things, of provisionally posited intrinsic nature, and of provisionally posited distinction; "as explained earlier in the Chapter on Genuine Reality" (Venerable Miào Jìng: fascicle 36). Master Cháng Bǎi: practising the four investigations is Yogācāra contemplation. Venerable Miào Jìng: the investigations are the cause, the genuine wisdoms the fruit.

Master Cháng Bǎi: saying the word "teacup" produces no actual teacup; once named, beings are often confined by the name and miss the thing itself. Venerable Miào Jìng: the rope exists; there is just no snake.
Master Cháng Bǎi's teacup is a good exercise. Look at something on your desk, and notice how quickly the name arrives and stands in for the thing.

quiz.q: What are the four kinds of establishing designations, and who can rightly establish them?
options: teaching, truths, principles, vehicles — only tathāgatas and bodhisattvas
quiz.why: Teaching, truths, principles, vehicles — only tathāgatas and bodhisattvas can rightly establish them; others only after hearing. Master Cháng Bǎi: others can only repeat what they heard, not establish it themselves.

quiz.q: "Compiled, arranged, and instituted in sequence" — what two readings do the lectures give?
options: Cháng Bǎi via Kuiji's notes: sūtra, treatise, vinaya — different from the commentary's reading; Miào Jìng: "arranged" is Abhidharma; the commentary says "in sequence" means undistorted
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: compiling refers to sūtras, arranging to treatises, instituting to vinaya (the Yogācāra notes' reading). Venerable Miào Jìng: arranging is Abhidharma; the commentary's author says "in sequence" means without distortion.

quiz.q: "Some establish a single truth" — meaning what?
options: the meaning of non-falsity — one truth only, no second
quiz.why: "Some establish a single truth: the meaning of non-falsity — only one truth, since there is no second." Venerable Miào Jìng: this praises suchness as not false, truly real.

quiz.q: Of the three truths — characteristic, language, function — what two does Venerable Miào Jìng say ordinary people move in?
options: characteristics and names — that's where ordinary people live; language requires names
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: we ordinary people deal in two things — characteristics and names; that's where we operate. The truth of language: without names, you couldn't speak.

quiz.q: Among the nine truths, how does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish "emptiness" and "no-self"?
options: no self in the aggregates is emptiness; no self apart from them is no-self
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: there is no self in form, feeling, perception, formations, consciousness — the truth of emptiness; apart from them there is also no self — the truth of no-self.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the first of the ten truths, "compelling suffering"?
options: suffering's pressure cuts like a knife
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: suffering presses like a knife cutting — hence "compelling." Venerable Miào Jìng: the ten are still the four truths, with suffering spelled out in more detail.

quiz.q: What is the first of the śrāvaka vehicle's seven aspects?
options: undistorted wisdom on the four truths
quiz.why: "First, undistorted wisdom on the four noble truths; then its basis, object, companions, function, provisions, and fruit." Venerable Miào Jìng: this wisdom isn't alone — as it develops, it has companions.

quiz.q: In the Mahāyāna's seven aspects, what does Venerable Miào Jìng say "this wisdom depends on"?
options: the buddha-nature within beings is the basis of this liberating wisdom
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the buddha-nature within beings is the basis of liberating wisdom. Master Cháng Bǎi: the seed of bodhicitta is its basis.

quiz.q: To attain four genuine wisdoms, which four investigations does the bodhisattva undertake?
options: names, things, provisional intrinsic nature, provisional distinction
quiz.why: Investigation of names, of things, of provisionally posited intrinsic nature, and of provisionally posited distinction. Master Cháng Bǎi: practising the four investigations is Yogācāra contemplation. Venerable Miào Jìng: the investigations are the cause, the genuine wisdoms the fruit.

quiz.q: For "investigating names," what examples do the lectures use?
options: Cháng Bǎi: saying "teacup" yields no teacup; names then confine us; Miào Jìng: all names are set up by the mind's discrimination and cannot stand on their own — empty of nature
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: saying the word "teacup" produces no actual teacup; once named, beings are often confined by the name and miss the thing itself. Venerable Miào Jìng: all names are set up by the mind's discrimination; they cannot exist on their own — empty of nature.
